analysis:
The PR changes two test files only. In EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift, the line 313 patch extends the stream-event switch from `.toolCall, .toolCallDelta` to include `.logprobs`. In GemmaToolCallLiveTests.swift (~line 264), `.info` becomes `.info, .logprobs`. Both updates only keep switches exhaustive after a new `.logprobs` case was added to MLXServerGenerationEvent. That case is defined in non-test sources outside this batch. These are test-harness changes; they alter no production code, authentication, attestation, encryption, cache or coordinator/provider wire behavior.

I also read the head-side context for the wiring tests, which cover heartbeat capacity, tool-choice validation, cacheScope/cacheSalt plumbing (T-041), cancellation, and KV fallback reasons. They exercise existing behavior and assert fail-closed outcomes: forced tool_choice rejection, forged schema metadata rejection, media bypass of the bridge, and the clamped heartbeat fallback reason. The tests continue to confirm that cacheSalt is passed through as the request's scope.

The tests do not weaken any threat-model mitigation. Remaining question for integration: how the new `.logprobs` event is produced and handled in production, in particular whether per-token logprobs are only emitted to the consumer over the encrypted response path and never in plaintext. This is outside the supplied evidence and should be checked in the source files that introduce the case, with the other batches. The test at lines ~1818-1853 only shows that logprobs entries are drained through a per-request channel in OpenAI shape. Because these are test-only changes, I report no finding.
